title: Revisiting Subject-Verb Agreement Mastery: The Effectiveness of Chatbots as Practice Tools
venue: Psychology and Education: A Multidisciplinary Journal
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether using ChatGPT as a chatbot-based practice tool can improve senior high school students’ mastery of subject-verb agreement. The problem addressed is persistent difficulty with grammar learning, especially subject-verb agreement, which the authors argue is often not sufficiently supported by traditional worksheets and teacher-led review. The study asks about students’ pretest performance, posttest performance after chatbot use, and whether the difference is statistically significant.

The intervention consisted of using the ChatGPT Free Plan as a practice partner for grammar exercises. After a pretest, students were oriented on how to access and interact with ChatGPT and then used it for one hour per day for five consecutive days under teacher supervision within the school compound. The outcome measure was a teacher-made 30-item multiple-choice test on subject-verb agreement administered before and after the intervention; the same items were reused in the posttest but rearranged. Because normality assumptions were not met, the authors analyzed pre/post change using a Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

Participants were 80 senior high school learners aged 16–18 from Lala Proper Integrated School in the Philippines, drawn from GAS, HUMSS, and TVL strands through purposive sampling based on language proficiency and teacher recommendation. The study took place during the second semester, second quarter of academic year 2024–2025, in a school-based setting during regular class scheduling.

The study concludes that ChatGPT use was associated with substantial short-term improvement in grammar performance. Mean scores increased from 15.6 ("Fair") to 21.4 ("Good"), with a mean difference of 6.00 points and a statistically significant Wilcoxon result (test statistic = 0.00, p < .001). The authors interpret this as evidence that ChatGPT can serve as an effective supplementary grammar-practice tool, though the design does not include a separate control group and outcomes were measured only immediately after the brief intervention.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study with a defined sample, validated instrument review, and reported reliability, but it lacks a control/comparison group and random assignment. The design supports causal inference only moderately, so it fits green rather than blue.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports a statistically significant and practically notable raw-score gain, but no standardized effect size is provided and the evidence comes from a single-group pre-post design using a teacher-made test reused at posttest. Because magnitude is not cleanly benchmarked and causal attribution remains somewhat uncertain, impact is best classified as yellow.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT Free Plan used as a supervised classroom practice partner for senior high school students to complete subject-verb agreement exercises for 1 hour daily over 5 consecutive days, with conversational grammar practice and immediate responses.
ChatGPT applied specifically as an English grammar support tool to practice and reinforce subject-verb agreement accuracy in sentence-level language tasks.

finding.finding_summary: In a one-group quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study of 80 senior high school students, scores on a 30-item teacher-made subject-verb agreement test increased from M=15.6 (SD=2.30) to M=21.4 (SD=2.62), a mean gain of 6.00 points after five days of ChatGPT practice. A Wilcoxon signed-rank test showed a highly significant pre-post improvement (test statistic=0.00, p<.001), with most students improving; no standardized effect size or confidence interval was reported.
